Sinigang na Baboy (Pork Sinigang) for 4

Servings: 4
Estimated time: 45–60 minutes

Ingredients
- 1.2–1.5 lb (600–700 g) pork ribs or bone-in pork shoulder, cut into 2–3 inch pieces
- 6 cups (1.4 L) water
- 1 medium onion, quartered
- 2 medium tomatoes, quartered
- 2–3 cloves garlic, minced (optional)
- 3 tablespoons tamarind paste (adjust to taste) or 1–2 sachets instant sinigang mix
- 1 cup daikon radish (labanos), sliced into thick half-moons
- 1 cup green beans (sitaw), cut into 2-inch pieces
- 1 small eggplant, cut into chunks
- 2–3 cups leafy greens (pak choi, pechay/Bok choy, or spinach)
- 2–3 tablespoons fish sauce (patis), plus more to taste
- Salt to taste (optional)

Steps
1) In a large pot, add pork and water. Bring to a boil, skim off foam, then reduce to a simmer.
2) Add onion, tomatoes, and garlic (if using). Simmer 30–40 minutes until pork is tender.
3) Stir in tamarind paste (or dissolve sinigang mix in a small amount of warm water first). Adjust sourness to taste.
4) Add daikon radish and green beans. Simmer 7–8 minutes.
5) Add eggplant. Simmer 3–5 minutes until tender.
6) Add leafy greens and simmer 1–2 minutes until wilted.
7) Season with fish sauce; taste and adjust salt or sourness as needed.
8) Serve hot with steamed rice. Optional: add a squeeze of lime for extra brightness.

Tips and variations
- If you’re using fresh tamarind, boil 2 cups water with 1 cup tamarind pulp, simmer to extract sourness, then strain and add the liquid to the pot.
- For seafood version, try sinigang na hipon (shrimp) or sinigang na isda (fish) using the same sour base; add shrimp or fish later so they don’t overcook.
- If the soup is too sour, add a little more water; if not sour enough, mix in a bit more tamarind paste.
- Serve with hot cooked rice for a classic pairing.
